Relative NN-Descent index

Source: R/indices_graph.R
RnnDescentIndex.Rd

Builds and prunes a navigable graph in one pass, skipping the separate refinement step NsgIndex pays for. r caps the out-degree, ef_search is the recall knob. On Gaussian benchmark data it tops out around 0.97 recall, so check it reaches what you need.

References

Ono & Matsui, ACM MM, 2023

RnnDescentIndex$new()

Build the index.

Usage

RnnDescentIndex$new(
  data,
  metric = c("euclidean", "sqeuclidean", "cosine", "manhattan"),
  s = 20L,
  r = 96L,
  t1 = 4L,
  t2 = 15L,
  n_trees = NULL,
  ef_search = NULL,
  k_search = NULL,
  seed = 42L,
  precision = c("float", "double"),
  .verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Numeric matrix or data.frame. Samples x features. An index pointer is also accepted; load_ann_index() uses that path.

metric

String. One of c("euclidean", "sqeuclidean", "cosine", "manhattan").

s

Integer. Neighbours sampled per node per local join.

r

Integer. Maximum out-degree after pruning.

t1

Integer. Outer iterations.

t2

Integer. Inner descent iterations per outer one.

n_trees

Integer or NULL. Random projection trees for the seed graph. NULL uses min(5 + n^0.25 / 2, 16).

ef_search

Integer or NULL. Beam width at query time. NULL uses 100. Can be changed after the build.

k_search

Integer or NULL. Neighbours expanded per hop. NULL uses 32, capped at r. Can be changed after the build.

seed

Integer. Fixes the seed graph and the sampling.

precision

String. "float" stores the data as f32, "double" as f64.

.verbose

Boolean. Print build progress from Rust.

RnnDescentIndex$clone()

The objects of this class are cloneable with this method.

Usage

RnnDescentIndex$clone(deep = FALSE)

Arguments

deep

Whether to make a deep clone.

Examples

x <- generate_clustered_data(1000L, 16L)$data
idx <- RnnDescentIndex$new(x)
res <- idx$predict(x[1:5, ], k = 10L)
